calls.title: Growthbook <> NovaKid - Intro
calls.summary: NovaKid (Vyacheslav Ryabukhin, technical lead, and Michael Lisovski, manager) discussed their need for advanced GrowthBook features like prerequisite feature dependencies and sticky buckets, which are missing in their current self-hosted setup. GrowthBook reps Daniel Wathne and Ryan McGurk explained enterprise pricing ($83/user/month + 20% platform fee) and proposed a tiered model with power and light users for the ~25-30 NovaKid team members. Next steps: Daniel will send a proposal with different user tier

calls.title: Growthbook <> Novakid - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The discussion centered on establishing two separate self-hosted infrastructure instances for Europe and China, necessitated by firewall restrictions and compliance needs. Michael Lisovski highlighted that the China instance requires isolation, while Dan Wathne confirmed that a self-hosted model could support full data separation under one corporate umbrella. Licensing is based on total seat counts rather than instances, ensuring cost-effectiveness. Key enterprise features essential for experimentation, including dynamic filtering and sticky bucketing, were emphasized as requiring the enterprise version. The proposed pricing model includes $700 per seat annually, with discounts available for case studies, while urgent timelines were set for decision-making to secure favorable terms before the quarter's end.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Novakid - Sync
calls.summary: The discussion focused on clarifying the meaning of 'instance' in the licensing agreement and its implications for multiple deployments under a single license. Dan explained that the license allows for unlimited organizations, which can be isolated, while Michael raised concerns about the need for separate installations. Various aspects of support were also addressed, including response times and SDK backward compatibility. Contract terms were outlined, emphasizing a 12-month duration without extensions and flexible payment options. Additionally, the audit process was defined as an annual review rather than an invasive technical audit. The meeting concluded with inquiries about non-production environments and their use under the license.
